neet_che_u12_t03_1.working: Ionisation isomers swap a ligand with the counter-ion, giving different ions in solution. In option 3, SO4^2- and Cl- exchange places. Option 1 is linkage, option 2 is geometrical and option 4 is hydrate isomerism.

neet_che_u12_t03_2.working: [CoBr2(en)2]+ has a trans form, which is achiral. Its cis form exists as a pair of enantiomers. Total stereoisomers = 1 + 2 = 3.

neet_che_u12_t03_3.working: [Cr(ox)3]3- is a tris-chelate with no mirror plane, giving delta and lambda forms, so it is chiral. The other three species each have a mirror plane.

neet_che_u12_t03_4.working: A: NO2 vs ONO is linkage (II). B: water inside vs outside the sphere is hydrate (IV). C: ligands exchanged between cation and anion is coordination (III). D: Cl and Br swap between sphere and counter-ion is ionisation (I).

neet_che_u12_t03_5.working: A is true: MA2B2C2 has 5 geometrical isomers, and the all-cis one is chiral, giving 6 stereoisomers. B is false: tetrahedral complexes show no cis-trans isomerism. C is true: square planar MABCD has 3 isomers. D is true by definition of fac. E is false: the trans isomer has a mirror plane. So A, C, D are correct.
